introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) From the table, state the identity element. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The identity $e$ satisfies $e*x=x*e=x$ for every $x$. In the completed table the row of $0$ is $0,1,2,3,4$ (the same as the header) and the column of $0$ is also $0,1,2,3,4$.

**The identity element is $0$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(c) From the table, state the inverse of each element. *[1 mark]*
(ii)(a) The transformation $T$ is defined by the matrix $M$, where $M=\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\1&3\end{pmatrix}$. Find the inverse of the matrix $M$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $M=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$, $M^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$.

Determinant: $\det M=2\times3-4\times1=6-4=2\neq0$, so $M$ is invertible.

$$M^{-1}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}3&-4\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac32&-2\\-\frac12&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Check: $M M^{-1}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\1&3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}3&-4\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}6-4&-8+8\\3-3&-4+6\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$.

**$M^{-1}=\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}3&-4\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Hence, or otherwise, find the point whose image is $(6,-5)$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
If the point $(x,y)$ has image $(6,-5)$ under $T$, then $M\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\-5\end{pmatrix}$, so

$$\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=M^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}6\\-5\end{pmatrix}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}3&-4\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}6\\-5\end{pmatrix}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}18+20\\-6-10\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}19\\-8\end{pmatrix}.$$

Check: $M\begin{pmatrix}19\\-8\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}38-32\\19-24\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\-5\end{pmatrix}$.

**The point is $(19,-8)$.**
